**Bangla Voice Clock** (বাংলা ভয়েস ক্লক) 0.5.0 puts every setting on one screen.

## New

- **A new window.** The clock and its dial of the day stay on the left, with **এখনই সময় শুনুন** and five sections: ঘোষণা (Announcements), কণ্ঠ ও শব্দ (Voice & sound), নীরব সময় (Quiet hours), টাইমার (Timer) and সাধারণ (General). The chosen section opens beside the clock, so nothing hides below the fold, even on a 1366×768 laptop. Labels now sit beside their controls. Narrow the window and the sections become tabs.
- **The top bar on GNOME.** On Debian, Fedora and other plain GNOME, **সাধারণ** offers to turn on GNOME's AppIndicator extension, so the icon and the time sit in the top bar as they do in the Mac menu bar. The `.deb` installs the extension. On Linux you can also choose the icon alone or the icon with the time.

## Fixed

- **Linux:** without a panel icon, the window no longer stays open all day. Closing it keeps the clock running out of sight (it says so once), and opening the app again brings it back; a **ঘড়ি বন্ধ করুন** (Quit) link appears under the sidebar. Starting at login no longer opens the window.

## Download

| | |
|---|---|
| **macOS** 12 or later, one universal app for Apple Silicon and Intel | `BanglaVoiceClock-v0.5.0-macos.dmg`: open it and drag **Bangla Voice Clock** onto **Applications**. It isn't signed yet: the first time, if macOS won't open it, go to **System Settings → Privacy & Security** and choose **Open Anyway**. Or use Homebrew: `brew install --cask saifulmd0/tap/bangla-voice-clock`. |
| **Windows** 10 or later (64-bit) | `BanglaVoiceClock-v0.5.0-windows-setup.exe`. SmartScreen may warn about an unknown publisher: choose **More info → Run anyway**. Or `BanglaVoiceClock-v0.5.0-windows-portable.zip`, which runs from any folder. On 0.3.0 or later, the app offers this update itself. |
| **Ubuntu, Debian, Mint** (64-bit) | `BanglaVoiceClock-v0.5.0-linux-amd64.deb`: run `sudo apt install ./BanglaVoiceClock-v0.5.0-linux-amd64.deb`, which also installs the top-bar extension. |
| **Any Linux** with Flatpak | `BanglaVoiceClock-v0.5.0-linux.flatpak`: run `flatpak install --user ./BanglaVoiceClock-v0.5.0-linux.flatpak`. |
| **Any Linux**, no install | `BanglaVoiceClock-v0.5.0-linux-x64.tar.gz`: extract it and run `bangla-voice-clock/bangla-voice-clock`. |

## Known limits

- Builds are not code-signed yet.
- The Linux version is 64-bit Intel/AMD only for now.
- An AppIndicator extension installed after you logged in starts at the next login.
